title: The same native Hamiltonian retains all sectors and a small residual-event condition
statement: The actual native prefix gauge and full-column dictionary give z_Gamma(s)=chi_EGamma(s) f_Gamma(s_T). Extract the occupied-hole factor exp(sum_T B_a q_a); owned-singleton cancellation leaves exp(beta delta_a), delta_a=integral_beta^infinity rho_a. A SINGLE positive history measure independent of ALL syndromes pointwise bounds f; separate integrated bounds at fixed syndrome do not justify a later supremum. The native source activity is q_native=K_max^b_c d_B^b_B exp(beta delta_max b_c)[exp(beta v_dict)-1]. Retain all clock levels, never-vacuum/wrapping paths and generic clock/bath matrix insertions. Exponentiating the native connected log creates independent multi-rod EVENT objects as a third species; their event-event factor is EXACTLY one even on overlap, so a hard core would change the actual trace. The defect-event row is <=2 E_gamma M and group-event row <=2 E_gamma(d_c m+M); the reverse event row costs rod count times small physical-top/source-contact rooted densities. Inflate EVERY rod activity by exp(gamma), including wraps, when computing E_gamma. Strict cold/source/event/tilt slack is required. E_gamma=O(beta J D eta^2)+tails must be SMALL. The finite-temperature bound v_dict<=beta^-1 log[1+q_star/(K_max^b_c d_B^b_B exp(beta delta_max b_c))] has no old extra exp(C beta J), but covers a strengthened region rather than the whole old native KP region. Colder targets may require smaller eta and larger peak native energy ratios. No fixed-H/fixed-v all-beta theorem or useful numerical tolerance follows; dictionary/hook constants may be prohibitive.
